bull: Extreme oversold: RSI 19.6, stochastic 9.4, price $258 near the lower Bollinger band ($244.90) — a reflex bounce toward the 20-day mid-band ($294.6, +14%) is technically possible.
Royalty/water model with no debt and high margins means the business itself is not distressed; a reversal of the Texas data-center moratorium debate would be a direct catalyst.
bear: Capitulation-style selling is still accelerating: -3.5% on the day on 3.9x normal volume, -11.7% in 5 days, -22.6% in 20 days — no sign of a low yet.
Structural downtrend: -52.6% from the 52-week high, 20.9% below SMA50 and 34.9% below SMA200, MACD deeply negative (-17.5), only 2.9% above the 52-week low.
ATR of $19.6 (7.6% of price) makes any entry a wide-stop, low-size trade.
TPL.summary: TPL tops the screener purely on oversold extremes, but the heaviest volume is arriving on down days and the stock is making fresh lows, which is what a falling knife looks like rather than a base. +10% needs a volume-backed reversal day and a reclaim of roughly $285-295; the downside scenario is a break of the 52-week low (~$251) triggering another leg toward $220-230. Wait for stabilisation before considering it.
TPL.key_risk: Break below the 52-week low on continued 3-4x volume, with Texas data-center/water-demand policy risk and weaker Permian activity as the fundamental driver.

bull: Deeply oversold: RSI 24.1, stochastic 0.5 and price $28.98 below the lower Bollinger band ($29.99) — statistically stretched, a snap-back to $31-33 is plausible.
Only 3.1% above the 52-week low (~$28.1), so a nearby reference level exists for a tight stop if a reversal day appears.
bear: Selling is intensifying, not fading: -4.6% today on 2x volume, -12.8% in 5 days, closing at the low of its range (stochastic 0.5).
Below SMA50 ($33.26, -12.9%) and SMA200 ($35.64, -18.7%), -39.4% from the 52-week high and only 3% above the 52-week low; no news in the knowledge base to explain or bound the decline.
IP.summary: International Paper is being sold hard on rising volume with no visible news to frame the move, and it is closing at the very bottom of its range below the lower Bollinger band. A +10% rebound requires a reclaim of ~$32 (inside the bands, toward the mid-band at $33.6); the downside case is a break of the 52-week low near $28.1 with cyclical packaging demand as the unknown. Unexplained high-volume declines deserve caution over bottom-fishing.
IP.key_risk: Unknown fundamental driver behind a high-volume breakdown — a guidance cut or demand shock in containerboard would extend the slide through the 52-week low.

bull: First real bounce attempt: +6.7% today from RSI 25 / stochastic 13.7, with 20-day momentum (-31.8%) far more stretched than 5-day (-9.2%) — selling pressure is decelerating.
Mean-reversion target is large: 20-day mid-band at $133 is +22% away, so even a partial retrace clears +10%.
bear: Bounce came on unremarkable volume (1.1x) — not yet a conviction reversal; price remains 32.9% below SMA50 and 36.8% below SMA200, -61.8% from the 52-week high.
Latest news is the failed Senate crypto market-structure vote, removing the regulatory-clarity catalyst; the stock is a high-beta proxy for crypto prices and ATR is $8.6 (7.9% of price).
COIN.summary: Coinbase shows the first signs of seller exhaustion with a 6.7% up-day from deeply oversold levels, and the distance to the mid-band makes a +10% relief move realistic. But volume did not confirm, the trend is severely broken, and the last known news (crypto bill failing) is negative; downside is a retest of the low near $101.7 and the lower band at $97.7. A speculative bounce candidate only, sized small.
COIN.key_risk: Crypto-price weakness and regulatory limbo push it back through the recent low (~$102), invalidating the bounce; very high volatility.

bull: Oversold after a -40% month: RSI 27.9, stochastic 1.4; still 302% above the 52-week low, so the long-term uptrend from last year's base is technically intact.
August news was strongly positive (bullish outlook, raised long-term targets) — if the NAND cycle thesis holds, the retrace offers a large rebound to the $126 mid-band.
bear: Momentum collapse with no stabilisation: -19.5% in 5 days, -40.1% in 20 days, -2.7% today, closing at the bottom of its range; MACD -21.2.
Lost both SMA50 ($170.7) and SMA200 ($160.7) by more than 40% — a sell-off of this size in a memory name usually signals a cycle/pricing reset that the stale August news does not capture.
ATR $12.9 is 13.7% of price — extreme volatility.
SNDK.summary: Sandisk has given back two thirds of its peak value and is still falling without a single reversal day, which points to a memory-cycle repricing rather than a routine pullback. +10% is only one ATR away and could come on any bounce, but there is no evidence of a floor; the lower Bollinger band at $75.5 (-20%) is the visible downside. The positive August outlook is too old to lean on.
SNDK.key_risk: NAND pricing/AI-storage demand downturn that the August guidance did not anticipate; 13.7% daily ATR makes stops unreliable.

bull: Most oversold reading in the set: RSI 18.4, stochastic 5.9; +2.7% today and 5-day loss (-10.4%) slowing versus 20-day (-32.2%).
Last fundamental news (Q2) was a raised 2026 outlook with the company split on track.
bear: -32% in 20 days with price 31-33% below both moving averages and only 3.6% above the 52-week low; today's bounce came on below-average volume (0.87x).

The quoted price ($8.10) and its moving averages look inconsistent with Corteva's historical trading range — possible data/corporate-action distortion (split/spin-off adjustment), so the technical picture may be unreliable.
CTVA.summary: On the numbers Corteva is extremely oversold and starting to stabilise, and its last known guidance was raised, which would normally argue for a mean-reversion bounce toward the $10.6 mid-band. However the price level itself looks questionable relative to the company's known range, and the planned separation could be distorting the series; confidence is low until the data is verified. Treat as not actionable rather than as a bargain.
CTVA.key_risk: Data integrity: price series may reflect a corporate action (split/spin-off) rather than a real 32% decline — any signal derived from it could be false.

bull: Orderly pullback rather than a collapse: RSI 43.1 with stochastic 8.5 and price at the lower Bollinger band ($63.14) — short-term oversold inside a narrow range (bands $63-72).
Low relative volatility (ATR $2.83, 4.4%) and normal volume (1.0x) — no sign of forced selling; mid-band at $67.7 and SMA50 at $68.8 are reachable (+6-7%).
bear: Sitting just 1.2% above the 52-week low and below SMA50 (-6.9%) and SMA200 (-11.4%); -8.5% over 5 days shows fresh weakness.
Last known catalyst was negative: Q3 bookings guidance disappointed and robotaxi spending is weighing on margins.
UBER.summary: Uber is the calmest chart among the screener names — a slow grind to the bottom of its range rather than a panic — and a bounce to the $68-69 SMA50 zone is realistic. A full +10% requires breaking above that resistance, which needs a new catalyst after the disappointing bookings guide. The risk is a clean break of the 52-week low (~$63.3) right beneath the current price, which would open $58-60.
UBER.key_risk: Break of the 52-week low ~1% below price; robotaxi capex and soft bookings growth keep sentiment capped.

bull: Oversold but structurally healthier than peers in the set: only 3.8% below SMA200 ($281) and -15% from the 52-week high; RSI 32.6, stochastic 6.4.
Selling stalled today (-0.16%) after a -9.9% week, with price just below the lower Bollinger band ($273.25) — a typical spot for a relief bounce to $281-288 (+4-6%).
bear: Sharp -9.9% 5-day drop on elevated volume (1.5x) took it below both SMA50 and SMA200 with no news in the knowledge base to explain it — likely sector/policy-driven.
MACD negative (-3.9) and no reversal day yet.
CI.summary: Cigna has had a fast, volume-backed drop through both moving averages, but the longer-term damage is limited and the selling paused today at the lower band. A bounce to the SMA200/SMA50 zone ($281-288) is the base case; +10% (~$297) would need the sector headwind to clear. Downside is a continuation toward the 52-week low near $254 (-6%). Worth watching for a confirmed up-day, not yet a buy.
CI.key_risk: Unexplained managed-care sell-off (policy/medical-cost risk) continuing toward the 52-week low at ~$254.

bull: Capitulation-level oversold: RSI 21.8, stochastic 6.3, price below the lower Bollinger band ($285.3) after a -20.3% week; first up-day today (+1.9%).
Gap-style drop leaves a large mean-reversion target — the mid-band at $331 is +20% away; high-quality recurring-revenue franchise.
bear: A -20% week is almost certainly an event (earnings/guidance) that the knowledge base does not contain — the cause is unknown and post-gap drift is commonly lower.
-59% from the 52-week high, 12.6% below SMA50 and 19.9% below SMA200; AI-disruption worries have been the persistent narrative in the news.
INTU.summary: Intuit dropped a fifth of its value in a week, most likely on an earnings or guidance shock that is not in our news feed, and is now extremely oversold below its lower band. A dead-cat bounce of +10% toward $300 is feasible given the stretch, but buying a gap-down without knowing the cause is a low-quality bet; the downside is a retest of the 52-week low near $250 (-9%). Needs a few days of base-building and fresh news before it earns conviction.
INTU.key_risk: Unknown event behind the -20% week; fundamental reset (guidance cut / AI competition) could push it to the 52-week low ~$250.

bull: Oversold: RSI 23.2, stochastic 6.1, price sitting exactly on the lower Bollinger band ($54.77); still 34.6% above the 52-week low.
Mean-reversion target is meaningful: the 20-day mid-band at $62.4 and SMA50 at $61.7 sit 13-14% above the current price.
bear: Persistent, accelerating distribution: -2.0% today, -11.2% in 5 days, -18.7% in 20 days on 1.5-2.0x volume — no reversal signal.
Below SMA50 ($61.7, -11.3%) and SMA200 ($63.8, -14.2%), MACD negative; with 34.6% of air down to the 52-week low there is no nearby support, and no news to explain the move.
LYB.summary: LyondellBasell is in a high-volume downtrend with every timeframe negative and no support until well below current prices. A +10% rebound to ~$60 would only bring it back to the underside of the broken SMA50 and requires a turn in chemical margins that nothing in the data suggests. Unlike the names near their 52-week lows, the downside here is wide open.
LYB.key_risk: Petrochemical margin/dividend-sustainability concerns driving continued institutional selling with no technical support nearby.

bull: Bounce attempt from the lower Bollinger band ($33.66): +2.6% today on 1.3x volume with RSI 34.2 and stochastic 10.6.
Mid-band at $37.6 and SMA50 at $36.6 give a +8-11% mean-reversion target if the bounce holds.
bear: Long-term trend is clearly down: 22.2% below SMA200 ($43.4), -49.9% from the 52-week high, only 5.6% above the 52-week low after a -11.8% week.
Last known news is negative for demand (Dick's Sporting Goods weakness highlighting Nike's struggles); turnaround has yet to show in numbers.
NKE.summary: Nike bounced off its lower band on slightly better volume, which sets up a tradeable move toward $36.6-37.6, roughly the +10% mark. But this remains a multi-quarter downtrend with weak wholesale-channel signals, and prior bounces have failed at the SMA50. Downside is a retest of the 52-week low near $32 (-5%). Acceptable risk/reward for a short-term trade only, not a trend change.
NKE.key_risk: Turnaround still unproven — weak consumer/wholesale demand sends it back to the 52-week low (~$32).

bull: Strongest momentum in the set: +43.4% in 20 days, +7.4% today, MACD strongly positive (+25.9), 20.6% above SMA50.
Fundamental backdrop from the last news cycle is powerful — 53% revenue growth and $1.9B quarterly revenue; a reclaim of SMA200 ($404, +8%) would confirm a trend reversal and open +10% and more.
bear: Overbought and extended: RSI 70.5, 20.6% above SMA50, with a -10% week inside the rally and today's rebound on thin volume (0.8x / 0.69x).
Still below SMA200 and -49% from the high; ATR of $31 (8.3%) means a routine pullback to the mid-band ($341) is -9%.
APP.summary: Scout candidate with real momentum: AppLovin has rallied 43% in a month on strong growth fundamentals, and a break above the SMA200 at ~$404 would be a genuine trend-change signal and the likely path to +10%. The problem is entry timing — RSI is above 70, volume is fading on the up-days, and the stock just showed a 10% weekly swing. Potential coming winner, but better bought on a pullback toward $340-350 or on a confirmed SMA200 breakout than chased here.
APP.key_risk: Rejection at the SMA200 (~$404) with a volatile retrace to the $310-340 zone; very high ATR and recurring short-seller/moat scrutiny.

bull: Confirmed uptrend: price 17.8% above SMA50 ($583) and 19.8% above SMA200 ($574), SMA50 above SMA200, MACD +32.8, only -10.8% from the 52-week high.
Healthy consolidation after a +20.5% month: RSI cooled to a neutral 54.3 and bb_position 61 on low volume (0.6-0.7x) — digestion, not distribution.
Fundamentals support it: raised 2026 EPS outlook on diagnostic growth and margin expansion.
bear: Extended versus its moving averages — a normal retrace to the mid-band ($664.5) is -3%, and a deeper one toward $620 would not break the trend but would hurt.
Premium-multiple name; low screener score (12) reflects that it is not cheap or oversold.
IDXX.summary: Scout candidate and the cleanest uptrend in the deep set: Idexx broke out by 20% in a month, sits above both rising moving averages and is now consolidating quietly with a neutral RSI. +10% (~$756) means a push to the upper Bollinger band and roughly the prior 52-week high, achievable on a continuation of the trend. The main downside is giving back part of the breakout toward $620-640; the trend stays intact above the mid-band at $664.
IDXX.key_risk: Valuation-driven pullback after a 20% run; a close below the 20-day mid-band (~$664) would signal the breakout is fading.

bull: Strong recovery: +26.7% in 20 days, positive across 1/5/20-day timeframes, MACD +2.7, 17.6% above SMA50 with RSI only 50.7 — momentum without being overbought.
Tight volatility (ATR $2.10, 3.0%) and Bollinger bands of $63.9-72.7 give a well-defined risk level; a break above SMA200 ($72.8, +4%) would confirm a trend change.
bear: Still below SMA200 and -34.9% from the 52-week high — the $72.7-72.8 zone (upper band + SMA200) is double resistance right overhead.
No fresh company-specific news; rally volume is average at best (0.8-1.1x).
PNR.summary: Scout candidate in a steady, low-volatility recovery: Pentair has climbed 27% in a month and is pressing toward the SMA200 at $72.80 with a neutral RSI. +10% (~$77) requires a clean break of that resistance, which would mark a real trend reversal; failure there likely means a drift back to the $64-66 area. Risk is well defined and volatility is low, making it one of the more attractive setups in the set, though confirmation is still pending.
PNR.key_risk: Rejection at the SMA200/upper-band resistance (~$72.8) and a fade back toward $64 in the absence of a news catalyst.

bull: Oversold with fading selling pressure: RSI 27.6, stochastic 9.2, +1.0% today on low volume (0.65x), close to the lower Bollinger band ($120.9).
Last fundamental news was strong — record Q2 revenue, earnings beat and raised full-year guidance; price is still 25% above the 52-week low.
bear: Downtrend intact: below SMA50 ($128.2) and SMA200 ($135.9), MACD negative, -11.7% in 20 days and -39.2% from the 52-week high.
No news since August to explain the slide; federal budget/contract risk may be what is being priced.
LDOS.summary: Current holding. Leidos remains oversold near its lower band, and the selling is drying up on low volume, so a relief move toward the SMA50 at $128 (+4%) is the near-term base case. A +10% move to ~$136 needs a reclaim of both the mid-band ($133.5) and SMA200, which would require a catalyst. The downside is a loss of $121 leading to a further 5-8% leg; hold with a stop discipline rather than add.
LDOS.key_risk: Close below the lower Bollinger band (~$121) continuing the downtrend; government budget/contract headlines.

bull: Solid long-term uptrend: 7.3% above SMA50 ($977) and 19.2% above SMA200 ($879), MACD +27.4, only -6.5% from the 52-week high.
Pullback is orderly: RSI 61.5, price exactly at the 20-day mid-band ($1,048) with stochastic reset to 37 on normal volume — a typical trend-support test.
bear: Short-term momentum has turned: -2.0% today and -5.1% over 5 days; a close below the mid-band opens $977-1,000 (-5-7%).
No recent news in the knowledge base; +10% would require a new all-time high above ~$1,121.
MCK.summary: Current holding. McKesson is the strongest trend among the holdings and is pulling back in an orderly way to its 20-day mid-band, a level where trending stocks commonly find support. +10% means breaking to new highs above $1,121, plausible if the defensive health-care distribution bid persists. The downside scenario is a deeper retrace to the SMA50 near $977; trend remains valid above that level.
MCK.key_risk: Loss of the 20-day mid-band (~$1,048) turning the pullback into a move to the SMA50 (~$977).

bull: Oversold and attempting to turn: RSI 23.9, +2.1% today on 1.1x volume, bb_position recovered to 29.6 and 5-day loss only -1.0% versus -7.7% over 20 days.
Low volatility (ATR $1.76, 2.3%) and defensive utility profile; Q2 earnings beat estimates.
bear: Only 2.3% above the 52-week low, below SMA50 ($80.6) and 11.5% below SMA200 ($87.8), MACD negative — the downtrend is not broken.
Texas data-center freeze threatens Oncor's ~300 GW load pipeline, a core part of the growth thesis.
SRE.summary: Current holding. Sempra is deeply oversold near its 52-week low but showed a constructive up-day with slowing downside momentum, so a move to the SMA50/mid-band at $80.6 (+4%) is realistic. +10% (~$85.5) would need the Texas data-center overhang on Oncor to ease. The downside is a break of the 52-week low near $76 (-2%), which should be treated as the exit trigger.
SRE.key_risk: Break of the 52-week low (~$76); Texas data-center moratorium reducing Oncor's load-growth outlook.

bull: Strong day in an intact uptrend: +4.6% on 1.15x volume, above SMA50 ($523, +3.0%) and SMA200 ($485, +11.0%), MACD positive, only -5.3% from the 52-week high.
Neutral RSI (54) and mid-band position (48.8) leave room to run to the upper band ($561) and the 52-week high (~$569) without being overbought.
Positive pipeline news flow (kidney-disease breakthrough) and analyst targets implying 20%+ upside.
bear: +10% (~$592) requires a breakout to new highs; the stock has been range-bound between roughly $517 and $561 for a month.
Pipeline/binary clinical and drug-pricing policy risk; ATR $15.3 (2.8%).
VRTX.summary: Current holding. Vertex is the best-positioned holding: a volume-backed 4.6% up-day inside a rising trend, with a neutral RSI and supportive pipeline news. A push through the upper band at $561 and the 52-week high near $569 would put +10% in reach. Downside is a fall back to the bottom of the range around $517-523 (-3-4%), where the SMA50 provides support.
VRTX.key_risk: Failure at the $561-569 resistance zone or a negative clinical/pricing headline sending it back to the SMA50 (~$523).

bull: Breakout-style strength: +4.8% today on 1.3x volume, positive on 1/5/20-day timeframes, 9.7% above SMA50 ($96.6) and 14.4% above SMA200 ($92.6), MACD +1.9.
RSI 62.2 — strong but not overbought; only -5.8% from the 52-week high (~$112.6), which coincides with the upper Bollinger band ($111.5).
bear: Upper band/52-week high at $111.5-112.6 is resistance just +5-6% above; +10% (~$116.6) needs a breakout to new highs.
ATR $4.3 (4.1%) means a retrace to the mid-band ($102.4, -3.4%) can happen quickly; news flow is thin and mixed.
ZBH.summary: Current holding. Zimmer Biomet is accelerating upward on rising volume with every timeframe positive and the trend structure (price > SMA50 > SMA200) fully bullish. The next test is the $111.5-112.6 resistance zone; clearing it would deliver +10%. The downside is a pullback to the mid-band near $102, which would still leave the uptrend intact.
ZBH.key_risk: Rejection at the 52-week high (~$112.6) and a retrace to the 20-day mid-band (~$102).

bull: Sharp rebound: +6.2% today, still 11.8% above SMA200 ($286.5) and 60.9% above the 52-week low — long-term uptrend intact.
RSI 45.4 and stochastic 52 are neutral; reclaiming the mid-band ($333.8, +4%) would point to the SMA50 at $357 (+11.6%).
bear: Bounce came on very low volume (0.6x) — weak confirmation; MACD still deeply negative (-14.6) after a -16.6% month.
Price is 10.4% below SMA50; the 5-day return is flat, so today only recovered earlier-week losses.
ZBRA.summary: Current holding. Zebra is in a correction within a longer-term uptrend: the 6% rebound is encouraging but came on thin volume and merely erased the week's losses. +10% requires reclaiming the mid-band at $334 and then running at the SMA50 near $357. The downside is a rollover toward the lower band and SMA200 at $285-287 (-10%); the mid-band is the level that decides which way this resolves.
ZBRA.key_risk: Low-volume bounce failing below the mid-band (~$334) and a slide to the SMA200/lower band (~$286).
